title: STH Weekly Newsletters You Want to Subscribe in Q3 2026
gist: ServeTheHome's founder describes the mechanics behind its free weekly newsletter and its Q3 2024-launched paid Substack, Axautik Group, which targets financial-community and data-center-infrastructure readers with deeper analyst content funded partly through corporate subscription budgets.

insights.claim: ServeTheHome launched a paid Substack called Axautik Group in Q3 2024 to supplement its free daily site with more detailed analyst-style content aimed at financial-community and data-center-infrastructure readers.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Signals a broader shift among independent hardware/trade publications toward gated, higher-detail analyst tiers monetized separately from ad-supported free content -- a model investors covering media/analyst-services businesses should track.
insights.quote: In Q3 2024, we launched our new Substack. The goal is to supplement what we have on STH with additional detail in the Substack.

insights.claim: ServeTheHome explicitly asks readers to redirect unused corporate industry-subscription budgets toward its Axautik Group Substack before quarter-end, framing enterprise expense allowances as a funding channel.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Shows a monetization tactic niche technical publishers can use -- targeting corporate research/subscription line items rather than relying solely on ads or consumer paywalls -- relevant for anyone evaluating trade-media or analyst-services revenue models.
insights.quote: If you want to support STH and your company purchases industry subscriptions, the new Substack is our offering.
insights.locator: If you want to support STH

insights.claim: The Axautik Group Substack published a piece explaining why Qualcomm's Cloud AI 100 accelerator is not more widely deployed, comparing it against common LPDDR memory options used by AMD, NVIDIA, and Apple.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Flags memory architecture (LPDDR choice) as a stated differentiator in AI inference accelerator competitiveness versus incumbents from AMD and NVIDIA -- worth following via the linked deep-dive for anyone tracking Qualcomm's data-center AI ambitions.
insights.quote: We compared it to common LPDDR options from AMD, NVIDIA, and Apple
insights.locator: Here is Why the Qualcomm Cloud AI 100 is Not Everywhere

insights.claim: ServeTheHome refuses to use newsletter signup pop-up overlays despite acknowledging they are effective at growing subscriber counts, because the site's founder believes they harm reader experience.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Illustrates a brand-differentiation choice (reader experience over growth-hacking) in a crowded tech-media landscape, relevant context for assessing audience loyalty and trust as intangible value in independent trade-media outlets.
insights.quote: We are not promoting the newsletter via overlays and pop-ups. Those are very effective, but they hurt our readers’ experience.
